newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: BANGLADESH, MALAYSIA LAUNCH CELL-PHONE VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: BANGLADESH, MALAYSIA LAUNCH CELL-PHONE VENTURE.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Monday spoke to her Malaysian counterpart Mahathir Mohammad via a cellular phone to launch a joint venture cellular telephone service called Aktel.
Telekom Malaysia owns 60 percent of the joint-venture company, Telekom Malaysia International Bangladesh Ltd (TMIB). The remaining 40 percent is owned by Bangladesh's A.K. Khan Group.
The official BSS news agency said Hasina dialed up the Malaysian prime minister in Kuala Lampur and had a seven-minute talk.
The two leaders exchanged good wishes and discussed bilateral relations during the conversation, BSS said.
Hasina called for more Malaysian investment in Bangladesh, the news agency said.
BSS said the company pledged to provide modern but cheap cellular services.
TMIB is one of three joint-venture cellular companies which the Bangladesh government allowed last year, opening up the telecommunications sector to private investment.
